learn.hook: In 1885, about seventy Indians met in Bombay to discuss their country's problems. Few could have guessed that their meeting would grow into a movement of crores.
points: The Indian National Congress was founded in December 1885 at Bombay. W. C. Bonnerjee presided over its first session, and A. O. Hume, a retired British official, helped set it up.

Early leaders such as Dadabhai Naoroji and Gopal Krishna Gokhale are called Moderates. They used petitions, speeches and newspapers to ask for reforms and wrote about the economic harm of British rule.
In 1905, Lord Curzon divided the province of Bengal. Many saw this as a move to divide people, and it sparked the Swadeshi movement: people boycotted British goods and used Indian-made goods instead.

Leaders who demanded stronger action, such as Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Lala Lajpat Rai and Bipin Chandra Pal (Lal-Bal-Pal), are often called Radicals. Tilak declared, 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it.'
Because of the strong protests, the partition of Bengal was cancelled in 1911.

example.q: Think it through: How did boycotting British cloth during the Swadeshi movement put pressure on the British?
steps: British mills earned huge profits by selling cloth in India.
When Indians stopped buying it, those sales fell.
Indian weavers and mills got more customers instead.
Lost profits and mass protest showed the British that Indians were united.
example.answer: It cut British profits, helped Indian industry and showed united public opposition.

learn.reallife: The word 'swadeshi', meaning 'of one's own country', is still used today when people choose locally made goods.

quiz.q: When was the Indian National Congress founded?
quiz.explain: It was founded in December 1885 at Bombay.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the dates of the national movement

quiz.q: Where was the first session of the Indian National Congress held?
quiz.explain: The first session met in Bombay in December 1885.

quiz.q: Who presided over the first session of the Congress?
quiz.explain: W. C. Bonnerjee was its first president.

quiz.q: Who said 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it'?
quiz.explain: Tilak made this declaration famous.

quiz.q: Which event of 1905 led to the Swadeshi movement?
quiz.explain: Lord Curzon's partition of Bengal sparked boycotts and swadeshi.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the causes of different movements

quiz.q: What did 'swadeshi' encourage people to do?
options: Use goods made in India and boycott British goods
quiz.explain: Swadeshi means 'of one's own country'.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what the term means

quiz.q: Leaders like Gokhale and Naoroji, who used petitions and speeches, are called:
quiz.explain: They believed in gradual reform through peaceful appeals.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the Moderates with the Radicals

quiz.q: The partition of Bengal took place in 1905 and was cancelled in 1911. How many years did it last?

teach.ask: Gappu asks, 'How did the freedom struggle begin?' Explain the early national movement to Gappu.
teach.praise: From a meeting in Bombay to swadeshi across Bengal: the movement had begun!
teach.nudge: When was the Congress founded? What happened in Bengal in 1905?

learn.hook: A thin man with a walking stick and a handful of salt shook the mighty British Empire. How?
points: Mahatma Gandhi returned to India from South Africa in 1915. He used satyagraha, the method of truth and non-violent resistance.
His first satyagrahas in India were for indigo farmers at Champaran in Bihar (1917), peasants of Kheda in Gujarat (1918) and mill workers of Ahmedabad (1918).

On 13 April 1919, British troops under General Dyer fired on a peaceful gathering at Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar, killing many people. The nation was deeply shocked. In 1920 Gandhi launched the Non-Cooperation Movement, which he withdrew in 1922 after violence at Chauri Chaura.

At its Lahore session in December 1929, the Congress demanded Purna Swaraj, complete independence. On 12 March 1930, Gandhi began the Salt March from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi to break the salt law, starting the Civil Disobedience Movement.
On 8 August 1942, the Quit India Movement was launched in Bombay with Gandhi's call 'Do or Die'.

example.q: Think it through: Why did Gandhi choose salt for his protest in 1930?
steps: Every person, rich or poor, needs salt.
The British had a monopoly on making salt and taxed it.
Making salt from sea water was simple, so anyone could break the law peacefully.
The protest united people across India in a simple, non-violent act.
example.answer: Salt was needed by all, the tax hurt the poor most, and anyone could break the salt law peacefully, so it united the whole country.

learn.reallife: Sabarmati Ashram in Ahmedabad and the Dandi memorial in Gujarat are visited by lakhs of people. 2 October, Gandhi's birthday, is also the International Day of Non-Violence.

quiz.q: When did Mahatma Gandhi return to India from South Africa?
quiz.explain: He returned in January 1915.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the dates of his life

quiz.q: Gandhi's first satyagraha in India was for indigo farmers at:
quiz.explain: Champaran in Bihar, in 1917.

quiz.q: On which date did the Jallianwala Bagh incident take place?
quiz.explain: Troops under General Dyer fired on a peaceful crowd in Amritsar on 13 April 1919.

quiz.q: Why did Gandhi withdraw the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1922?
options: Because the British agreed to all demands
Because of violence at Chauri Chaura
quiz.explain: Gandhi insisted the movement must stay non-violent.
quiz.mistake: Does not connect the withdrawal to non-violence

quiz.q: What did 'Purna Swaraj', demanded in 1929, mean?
quiz.explain: Purna means 'complete'; Swaraj means 'self-rule'.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the meaning of the term

quiz.q: The Salt March went from Sabarmati Ashram to:
quiz.explain: Gandhi walked to Dandi on the Gujarat coast, reaching it on 6 April 1930.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up places of different movements

quiz.q: Which movement was launched on 8 August 1942 with the call 'Do or Die'?
quiz.explain: Gandhi gave this call in Bombay at the launch of the Quit India Movement.

quiz.q: How many years passed between the Salt March (1930) and the Quit India Movement (1942)?

teach.ask: Gappu asks, 'How did Gandhi fight without weapons?' Explain satyagraha and Gandhi's movements to Gappu.
teach.praise: No weapons, just truth and courage! Gappu salutes satyagraha.
teach.nudge: What was Gandhi's method? Can you name his big movements?

learn.hook: The freedom struggle had many heroes: speakers, writers, soldiers, farmers, students and women from every corner of India.
points: Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru were young revolutionaries who were hanged by the British on 23 March 1931. 23 March is observed as Shaheed Diwas in their memory. Chandrashekhar Azad was another fearless revolutionary.
Subhas Chandra Bose led the Indian National Army (Azad Hind Fauj) with the call 'Dilli Chalo'. He is also remembered for the words 'Give me blood, and I will give you freedom!'
Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel led the Bardoli satyagraha of farmers in 1928. After independence, he played the key role in uniting the princely states with India.

Women leaders included Sarojini Naidu, the first Indian woman to preside over the Congress, and Aruna Asaf Ali, who hoisted the flag in Bombay at the start of the Quit India Movement. Rani Gaidinliu led resistance in the north-east.

India became independent on 15 August 1947, though the country was partitioned and India and Pakistan were formed. Jawaharlal Nehru became the first Prime Minister, and Dr B. R. Ambedkar chaired the committee that drafted the Constitution.

example.q: Think it through: Why do historians say the freedom struggle was a 'people's movement' and not the work of one leader?
steps: Leaders followed different paths: peaceful satyagraha, revolutionary action and the INA.
Farmers, workers, students and women joined protests across the country.
People from every region and community took part.
Together, this pressure made it impossible for British rule to continue.
example.answer: Because many leaders and lakhs of ordinary people from every region took part in different ways, and their combined effort won freedom.

learn.reallife: Every year on 15 August, the Prime Minister hoists the national flag at the Red Fort in Delhi, and 23 January, Netaji's birthday, is celebrated as Parakram Diwas.

games.title: True or false?
items: Power was transferred at midnight on 14–15 August 1947.
Subhas Chandra Bose led the Indian National Army.
He led the INA (Azad Hind Fauj) during the Second World War.
Jawaharlal Nehru was independent India's first President.
Nehru was the first Prime Minister; Dr Rajendra Prasad was the first President.
Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru were hanged on 23 March 1931.
The day is remembered as Shaheed Diwas.
Only people from one region took part in the freedom struggle.
People from every region and community took part.

quiz.q: Which leader gave the call 'Dilli Chalo'?
quiz.explain: Netaji gave this call to the soldiers of the INA.

quiz.q: Who led the Bardoli satyagraha of 1928?
quiz.explain: The success at Bardoli earned him the title 'Sardar'.

quiz.q: Who played the key role in uniting the princely states with India after independence?
quiz.explain: Patel, as Home Minister, persuaded the princely states to join India.
quiz.mistake: Does not know Patel's role after 1947

quiz.q: On which date were Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru hanged?
quiz.explain: 23 March is remembered as Shaheed Diwas.

quiz.q: Who was the first Indian woman to preside over the Indian National Congress?
quiz.explain: Sarojini Naidu presided over the Congress session of 1925.

quiz.q: Who was the first Prime Minister of independent India?
quiz.explain: Nehru became Prime Minister on 15 August 1947.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the first Prime Minister with the first President

quiz.q: Who chaired the Drafting Committee of the Indian Constitution?
quiz.explain: Dr Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the roles of national leaders

quiz.q: India became independent in 1947. How many years after the founding of the Congress (1885) was this?

teach.ask: Gappu thinks only one person won India's freedom. Explain to Gappu how many leaders and people played a part.
teach.praise: So many heroes, one dream! Thank you, freedom fighters.
teach.nudge: Can you name some leaders besides Gandhi? When did India become free?
